subject: Economics
why: The live database holds 25 broad Economics topics, most of them a whole syllabus topic or several joined together, so a student cannot see which part of a topic they are weak on. Version 1.0 is the first two-level taxonomy: parent topics at the grain of the numbered topics in the WAEC and JAMB syllabi, and subtopics at the grain of their sub-areas, with one subtopic citing both exams wherever they cover the same content. It was checked against the 39 surviving items of the 2024 UTME paper; every one lands on a single subtopic, and the four that test content outside both syllabi are placed and explained in the scope rule. No WASSCE paper was available to check against, so the subtopics cited only to WAEC have not yet been tested on a real WASSCE paper. Every one of the 25 legacy database topics is folded in. Nothing in the database is changed by this file. Version 1.1 revises 1.0 from its coverage map and its placement test on 80 UTME questions from 2014 to 2024: it gives the missing concepts a home by widening existing subtopics and adds sorting rules on every border the two models split on. No subtopic is added, split or merged, so every placement made against 1.0 stays valid.

documents.provenance_note: Third-party mirror, the same one used for Biology. PDF dated 2015-09-24, author field awajis.com. Not fetched from a WAEC domain directly.

documents.document: JAMB UTME Economics syllabus, 23 topics with objectives, labelled the 2026 version
documents.provenance_note: Third-party reproduction. The official copy is on jamb.gov.ng behind its syllabus portal. Topic list cross-checked against a second copy on kofastudy.com.

source.scope_rule: Neither syllabus limits the objective paper to part of its content: WAEC Paper 1 is fifty multiple choice questions on the whole syllabus, and the UTME is objective throughout. So every topic in both syllabi is placed. The 2024 UTME paper also tested four things outside both syllabi, and each is placed where it sits most naturally rather than given a subtopic of its own: economists and the history of economic thought (Q27, Luca Paciolo as the odd one out among economists) under basics.meaning; the theorists of international trade (Q5, Smith and Ricardo) under trade.basis; current Nigerian office holders and institutions (Q32, the CBN governor; Q33, the Bank of Industry headquarters) under financial.central-bank and financial.types; and oligopoly and duopoly (Q15 options), which neither syllabus names, under markets.imperfect. The placement test on UTME papers from 2014 to 2024 found more content outside both syllabi, placed the same way: stock and flow variables (2019 Q29) under tools.methods; the Phillips curve (2020 Q39) under inflation.effects-control; open and closed economies (2020 Q38) under trade.basis; the UN specialised agencies such as WHO under organisations.others; and the unbundling and sale of the power sector (NEPA, PHCN) under business.privatisation. The scheme of work adds welfarism, globalisation, lessons from the Asian Tigers and Japan, and the MDGs, NEEDS and Vision 20:2020, each named in the covers line of the subtopic that holds it. Where one syllabus goes further than the other, the subtopic cites only that syllabus and the other is null. JAMB only: scientific method, measures of dispersion, indifference curves, consumer surplus, isoquants, rent, interest and profit, the circular flow, consumption and saving, the multiplier, the consumer price index, deflation, monetary policy and economic reforms. WAEC only: distributive trade, meaning and types of industry, terms of trade, commercial policy and protection, and the levels of economic integration.

how_to_use: Place a question by what a student must know or do to answer it, not by words in the stem. A question that mentions a tax but asks for an elasticity coefficient goes under elasticity; one that mentions elasticity but asks who bears a tax goes under tax incidence. A question that makes the student calculate goes where the calculation is taught. Read the covers line before choosing; where two subtopics look close, the covers line says which one wins.

topics.name: Economics as a science and basic concepts

subtopics.name: Meaning and scope of economics
subtopics.covers: Definitions of economics (Smith, Marshall, Robbins), economics as a social science, micro and macroeconomics, and the major economists and what each is known for. Tested in 2024 UTME Q27. A question about a trade theorist's theory goes to trade.basis.

subtopics.name: Wants, scarcity, choice and opportunity cost
subtopics.covers: Human wants, scarcity, choice, scale of preference, rationality and opportunity cost, including identifying the opportunity cost in a given choice (2024 UTME Q37). Scarcity as the basic economic problem goes here; the questions of what, how and for whom to produce go to systems.economic-problems.

subtopics.name: Production possibility curve
subtopics.covers: Drawing and reading the production possibility curve: points inside, on and outside it, efficiency, opportunity cost along it, its shape, and what shifts it outward or inward. Tested in 2024 UTME Q34 to Q36. Any question built on a PPC diagram goes here, even when it asks about opportunity cost.

subtopics.name: Economic activities and types of production
subtopics.covers: Production, distribution and consumption as economic activities; primary, secondary and tertiary production (extractive, manufacturing, construction, services, direct and indirect production); and the relative contribution of each sector to output, employment, savings, investment and foreign exchange. A question on productivity or on TP, AP and MP goes to production.productivity. Classifying manufacturing or construction as secondary production goes here; the role and problems of Nigeria's manufacturing and construction industries go to industry.development.

subtopics.name: Capitalism, socialism and mixed economy
subtopics.covers: Free enterprise, centrally planned and mixed economies, and welfarism (the welfare state): their basic features, advantages and disadvantages, and identifying a system from a description, even when the description is that prices decide what is produced. The functions of the price mechanism itself go to price.market-system. Whether an economy is open or closed is a question of trade and goes to trade.basis, even when the options mix it with capitalist, socialist or mixed.

subtopics.name: Basic economic problems and how each system solves them
subtopics.covers: What to produce, how to produce, for whom to produce and efficiency of resource use, and how the price mechanism, central planning or a mix answers each. A question that only asks what scarcity is goes to basics.scarcity-choice. A question on how a system uses the price mechanism to answer what, how and for whom goes here; one on the functions of the price mechanism in a market (rationing, allocating, signalling) goes to price.market-system; one that asks which system a description fits goes to systems.types.

subtopics.name: Economic reforms in Nigeria
subtopics.covers: Contemporary reforms such as deregulation, banking sector consolidation and the cashless policy, and what they mean for the economic system. Privatisation and commercialisation go to business.privatisation.

topics.name: Methods and tools of economic analysis

subtopics.name: Scientific method and basic concepts of analysis
subtopics.covers: Inductive and deductive reasoning, and positive and normative statements, including classifying a given statement; and the basic concepts of economic analysis: variables and functions, and stock and flow variables (a stock is measured at a point in time, a flow over a period), which neither syllabus names but the 2019 UTME tested (Q29). Whether a quantity such as wealth, capital or income is a stock or a flow goes here, not to national-income.concepts.

subtopics.name: Tables, charts and graphs
subtopics.covers: Reading and drawing tables, bar charts, pie charts, histograms and line graphs, calculating the angle or share in a pie chart, and the merits and demerits of each. A graph that tests an economic concept (a demand curve, a PPC) goes to that concept.

subtopics.name: Mean, median and mode
subtopics.covers: Calculating the arithmetic mean, median and mode of raw, tabulated or grouped data, and their merits and demerits. Tested in 2024 UTME Q22 to Q24.

subtopics.name: Range, variance and standard deviation
subtopics.covers: Calculating and interpreting the range, variance and standard deviation. Tested in 2024 UTME Q25.

subtopics.name: Law of demand, demand schedule and curve
subtopics.covers: Meaning of demand, effective demand, the law of demand, individual and market demand schedules and curves, demand equations and solving one for price or quantity at a given value, and exceptional demand curves (Giffen, Veblen and ostentatious goods, expectation of price change). Tested in 2024 UTME Q19. A question that asks about the laws of demand and supply together goes here. Setting the demand and supply equations equal to find equilibrium goes to price.equilibrium.

subtopics.name: Determinants of demand and shifts in demand
subtopics.covers: Factors that determine demand (price, prices of other goods, income, taste, expectations, population) and the difference between a change in quantity demanded (movement along the curve) and a change in demand (shift of the curve).

subtopics.name: Types of demand
subtopics.covers: Derived, composite, joint (complementary) and competitive demand, and how a price change of one good affects the demand for a related good (2024 UTME Q1). If the question asks for a cross elasticity coefficient or its sign, it goes to demand.elasticity.

subtopics.name: Measuring elasticity of demand
subtopics.covers: Price, income and cross elasticity of demand: calculating the coefficient, interpreting it, and the types (perfectly elastic, elastic, unitary, inelastic, perfectly inelastic) and their curves. Tested in 2024 UTME Q40.

subtopics.name: Determinants and importance of elasticity of demand
subtopics.covers: Why demand for a good is elastic or inelastic (substitutes, necessity, share of income, habit, time) and why elasticity matters to consumers, producers (pricing, total revenue) and government. A question about who bears a tax goes to public-finance.incidence; one about devaluation and import demand goes to bop.exchange-rate.

subtopics.name: Law of supply, supply schedule and curve
subtopics.covers: Meaning of supply, the law of supply, individual and market supply schedules and curves, supply equations and solving one for price or quantity at a given value (2023 UTME Q37), and exceptional supply curves such as the backward-bending supply of labour. Tested in 2024 UTME Q20. A question that asks about the laws of demand and supply together goes to demand.law. Setting the demand and supply equations equal to find equilibrium goes to price.equilibrium.

subtopics.name: Determinants of supply and shifts in supply
subtopics.covers: Factors that determine supply (price, input costs, technology, prices of other goods, weather, government policy) and the difference between a change in quantity supplied and a change in supply.

subtopics.name: Types of supply
subtopics.covers: Joint (complementary), competitive and composite supply, with examples.

subtopics.name: Elasticity of supply
subtopics.covers: Calculating and interpreting elasticity of supply, its types and curves, its determinants (time, spare capacity, perishability) and its importance to producers and government.

subtopics.name: Utility and diminishing marginal utility
subtopics.covers: Cardinal and ordinal utility, total, average and marginal utility and calculating them from a schedule, the law of diminishing marginal utility, and how marginal utility explains the downward-sloping demand curve.

subtopics.name: Consumer equilibrium using marginal utility
subtopics.covers: The equi-marginal condition (MUa/Pa equals MUb/Pb), finding the equilibrium combination from a table, and the effect of a price change on that equilibrium. Equilibrium found with an indifference map goes to consumer.indifference.

subtopics.name: Indifference curves and budget line
subtopics.covers: Indifference curves and their properties, the budget line and its shifts, equilibrium where the budget line touches an indifference curve, and income and substitution effects. Tested in 2024 UTME Q10. Equilibrium found by comparing marginal utility per naira goes to consumer.equilibrium. A curve of inputs giving equal output is an isoquant and goes to production.producer-equilibrium.

subtopics.name: Consumer surplus
subtopics.covers: Meaning and calculation of consumer surplus and its applications, such as price discrimination and taxation.

subtopics.name: The market and the price system
subtopics.covers: Meaning of market and price, types of market, and the functions of the price system (rationing, allocating resources, signalling). A question on what the price mechanism does in a market goes here; one on how an economic system uses it to answer what, how and for whom goes to systems.economic-problems; one that asks which system a description fits goes to systems.types.

subtopics.name: Equilibrium price and quantity
subtopics.covers: Finding equilibrium price and quantity from a schedule, a graph or demand and supply equations, excess demand and excess supply, and equilibrium in factor markets. Tested in 2024 UTME Q38 and Q39. A question that solves only the demand or only the supply equation at a given price or quantity goes to demand.law or supply.law, even inside a set of questions on the same equations.

subtopics.name: Effects of changes in demand and supply on equilibrium
subtopics.covers: Predicting what happens to equilibrium price and quantity when demand, supply or both shift. A question that only asks what causes a shift goes to demand.determinants or supply.determinants.

subtopics.name: Price control: maximum and minimum prices
subtopics.covers: Maximum (ceiling) and minimum (floor) price legislation, where each is set relative to equilibrium, and their effects: shortages, surpluses, rationing, queues and the black market. Tested in 2024 UTME Q31. Minimum agricultural prices as a farm policy go to agriculture.marketing-policy.

subtopics.name: Land, labour, capital and entrepreneur
subtopics.covers: Meaning, features and importance of each factor of production, forms of capital, functions of the entrepreneur, and which reward goes to which factor. Mobility and efficiency of labour go to labour.force.

subtopics.name: Rent, interest and profit
subtopics.covers: How rent, interest and profit are determined, economic rent and transfer earnings, normal and supernormal profit as a reward, and the liquidity preference theory of interest. Wages go to labour.wages; the motives for holding money go to money.demand-supply.

subtopics.name: Division of labour and specialisation
subtopics.covers: Meaning of division of labour and specialisation, their advantages and disadvantages, and what limits them (size of market, nature of product).

subtopics.name: Total, average and marginal product
subtopics.covers: Calculating TP, AP and MP from a schedule, the relationship between them, the law of variable proportions (diminishing returns), and factors affecting productivity. Tested in 2024 UTME Q12.

subtopics.name: Scale of production and size of firms
subtopics.covers: Internal and external economies and diseconomies of scale, production functions and returns to scale (increasing, constant, decreasing), and the factors that determine the size of a firm.

subtopics.name: Isoquants and producer equilibrium
subtopics.covers: Isoquants and isocost lines, and the least-cost combination of inputs by isoquant-isocost and marginal analysis. Tested in 2024 UTME Q11.

subtopics.name: Fixed, variable, total, average and marginal cost
subtopics.covers: Meaning of each cost concept and calculating one from the others in a table or from a cost function.

subtopics.name: Short-run and long-run costs
subtopics.covers: What the short run and long run are (2024 UTME Q13), the shapes of short-run and long-run cost curves, and why the marginal cost curve above average variable cost is the firm's supply curve.

subtopics.name: Economist's and accountant's view of cost
subtopics.covers: Opportunity (implicit) cost against money (explicit) cost, and economic against accounting profit.

subtopics.name: Revenue concepts
subtopics.covers: Total, average and marginal revenue, calculating them from a table, and marginal revenue product. A question that uses marginal revenue product to explain wages goes to labour.wages.

subtopics.name: Perfect competition
subtopics.covers: Assumptions and features of perfect competition, why price equals AR equals MR, short-run and long-run equilibrium, and reading the curves on a perfect competition diagram (2024 UTME Q15, Q17, Q18).

subtopics.name: Monopoly and price discrimination
subtopics.covers: Sources and features of monopoly, the monopolist's equilibrium, control of monopoly, and price discrimination: its conditions, forms and effects.

subtopics.name: Monopolistic competition and oligopoly
subtopics.covers: Features and short-run and long-run equilibrium of monopolistic competition, product differentiation and advertising, and oligopoly and duopoly, which neither syllabus names but the 2024 UTME used as options.

subtopics.name: Profit, loss and shut-down of firms
subtopics.covers: Normal profit, supernormal profit and loss, reading the profit or loss area on a cost and revenue diagram (2024 UTME Q16), and the break-even and shut-down conditions in each market. A question that asks which market a diagram shows goes to that market.

subtopics.name: Private business organisations
subtopics.covers: Sole proprietorship, partnership, private and public limited companies and co-operative societies: their features, advantages, disadvantages and problems.

subtopics.name: Public enterprises
subtopics.covers: Statutory corporations and joint ventures: why government sets them up, their features and their problems.

subtopics.name: Privatisation, commercialisation and indigenisation
subtopics.covers: Privatisation and commercialisation as solutions to the problems of public enterprises, the difference between them and their merits and demerits, indigenisation and nationalisation policies, and Nigerian cases such as the unbundling of NEPA into PHCN and the sale of its successor companies, which neither syllabus names but UTME papers test.

subtopics.name: Sources of funds and management of firms
subtopics.covers: Internal and external sources of funds: ordinary and preference shares, debentures, loans, overdrafts and retained profit, and how businesses are managed and controlled. Tested in 2024 UTME Q8. A question on where a firm goes to raise funds goes here, even when the answer is the stock exchange; how the stock exchange works goes to financial.markets.

subtopics.name: Channels of distribution
subtopics.covers: The chain from producer to consumer, and the roles of producers, wholesalers, retailers and co-operatives, including arguments for eliminating the middleman.

subtopics.name: Problems of distribution and the role of government
subtopics.covers: Problems of distribution in West Africa (transport, storage, hoarding, too many middlemen) and their solutions, and government agencies in product distribution.

subtopics.name: Population theories
subtopics.covers: The meaning of population and its basic terms, the Malthusian theory and its criticisms, the demographic transition theory, and their relevance to Nigeria. Optimum population as a size goes to population.size-growth.

subtopics.name: Census
subtopics.covers: What a census is, how often it is held (2024 UTME Q26), its importance, and the problems of conducting one in Nigeria.

subtopics.name: Population size, growth and migration
subtopics.covers: Birth rate, death rate and migration as determinants of size and growth, rural-urban migration, under-population, optimum population and over-population, and population policy and economic development. Why people move into or out of an area (push and pull factors) goes here; how a population is spread across areas goes to population.structure. The meaning of population goes to population.theories.

subtopics.name: Population structure and distribution
subtopics.covers: Age, sex, occupational and geographical distribution, the dependency ratio, and population pyramids. How a population is spread across areas goes here; why people move into or out of an area goes to population.size-growth.

subtopics.name: Labour force, efficiency and mobility
subtopics.covers: The labour force and what determines its size, human capital, efficiency of labour, and occupational and geographical mobility of labour and other factors, and what hinders it.

subtopics.name: Wage determination and trade unions
subtopics.covers: Supply of and demand for labour, how wages are determined, the marginal productivity theory of wages, trade unions and employers' associations, collective bargaining, and government wage policy such as the minimum wage.

subtopics.name: Unemployment and underemployment
subtopics.covers: Types of unemployment (structural, frictional, seasonal, cyclical, disguised), underemployment, their causes in Nigeria and solutions. The Phillips curve, which links unemployment to inflation, goes to inflation.effects-control.

topics.name: Agriculture
topics.part: The Nigerian and West African economy

subtopics.name: Structure and systems of agriculture
subtopics.covers: Food crops, export (cash) crops, livestock, fisheries and forestry, and peasant, commercial, co-operative and state farming and their features.

subtopics.name: Importance of agriculture to the economy
subtopics.covers: Agriculture as a source of food, employment (the largest employer, 2024 UTME Q2), raw materials, foreign exchange and government revenue, and the link between agriculture and industry.

subtopics.name: Marketing, agricultural policies and price instability
subtopics.covers: Marketing of farm produce and commodity (marketing) boards, agricultural policies and programmes such as guaranteed minimum prices and subsidies, and the causes, effects and solutions of unstable farm incomes, including buffer stocks.

subtopics.name: Problems of agriculture and remedies
subtopics.covers: Why agricultural output is low (land tenure, poor tools, finance, storage, rural-urban migration as it affects farming, 2024 UTME Q6) and how the problems can be solved.

topics.name: Industry and industrialisation
topics.part: The Nigerian and West African economy

subtopics.name: Meaning and types of industry
subtopics.covers: Meaning and types of industry, and the terms plant, firm, industry and industrial estate. Primary, secondary and tertiary production as sectors go to basics.economic-activities.

subtopics.name: Location and localisation of industry
subtopics.covers: The difference between location and localisation, the factors that influence where an industry sits, and the advantages and disadvantages of localisation.

subtopics.name: Strategies of industrialisation
subtopics.covers: Import substitution, export promotion, and other industrialisation strategies used in Nigeria, with their merits and demerits.

subtopics.name: Industrialisation and economic development
subtopics.covers: The role of industry in development, the problems of industrialising in Nigeria and West Africa, the role and problems of Nigeria's manufacturing and construction industries, and the link between agricultural and industrial development. Classifying manufacturing or construction as secondary production goes to basics.economic-activities.

topics.name: Natural resources and the economy
topics.part: The Nigerian and West African economy

subtopics.name: Development of major natural resources
subtopics.covers: Where petroleum, gold, diamond, tin, timber, groundnut and other resources are found and how they were developed, their positive and negative effects on West African economies, environmental damage from exploitation, and how it can be controlled. Challenges of exploiting natural resources in general go here; problems particular to the oil and gas industry go to natural-resources.oil.

subtopics.name: The oil sector
subtopics.covers: Contributions of the oil and non-oil sectors, linkage effects, upstream and downstream activities, the roles of NNPC and OPEC, and the problems of the oil and gas industry (pipeline vandalism and oil theft, low refining capacity and fuel imports, oil price swings, unrest in the Niger Delta). Every OPEC question goes here, including its founding and membership, because both syllabi treat OPEC through oil. Challenges of exploiting natural resources in general go to natural-resources.major.

topics.name: Economic growth, development and planning
topics.part: The Nigerian and West African economy

subtopics.name: Growth and development and their indicators
subtopics.covers: The difference between economic growth and economic development, and indicators such as per capita income, life expectancy, literacy and the human development index. Per capita income as one indicator of development set against others goes here; per capita income as a measure of living standards over time or between countries goes to national-income.uses.

subtopics.name: Features and problems of developing countries
subtopics.covers: Factors that promote or hinder growth and development, the lessons Nigeria can draw from the development of the Asian Tigers, Japan, Europe and America, and the characteristics and problems of developing countries, Nigeria in particular, including dependence on one main export (a mono-product economy). The mono-product economy as a feature or problem goes here; what Nigeria exports and to whom goes to trade.structure.

subtopics.name: Development planning
subtopics.covers: Objectives and elements of a development plan, types of plan (short, medium, long term, rolling), Nigeria's development plans and programmes such as the MDGs, NEEDS and Vision 20:2020, and the problems of planning.

subtopics.name: National income concepts
subtopics.covers: GDP, GNP, NNP, national income, per capita income, depreciation and net factor income from abroad, and calculating one from another. Whether a quantity is a stock or a flow goes to tools.methods.

subtopics.name: Measuring national income and its problems
subtopics.covers: Output, income and expenditure methods, double counting, and the problems of measurement such as unrecorded subsistence output and unpaid services (2024 UTME Q21). A question that adds up consumption, investment, government spending and net exports with no propensity given goes here; one that gives an MPC or MPS and asks for national income goes to national-income.multiplier.

subtopics.name: Uses and limitations of national income data
subtopics.covers: Using national income figures to compare living standards over time and between countries, why such comparisons mislead, and trends and structure of national income. Per capita income as a measure of living standards goes here; per capita income as one indicator of development set against others such as life expectancy or the HDI goes to development.meaning; calculating it goes to national-income.concepts.

subtopics.name: Circular flow of income
subtopics.covers: The two-sector and three-sector circular flow models, injections and leakages. What an open or closed economy is goes to trade.basis.

subtopics.name: Consumption, saving and investment
subtopics.covers: Meaning and determinants of consumption, saving and investment, and the average and marginal propensities to consume and save.

subtopics.name: The multiplier and equilibrium national income
subtopics.covers: Calculating the multiplier from MPC or MPS, its effect on income, and elementary determination of equilibrium national income. A question that only asks for MPC goes to national-income.consumption-saving. A national income question that gives an MPC or MPS goes here, even when it also lists consumption, investment, government spending and trade figures (2017 UTME Q12); adding up expenditure with no propensity given goes to national-income.measurement.

subtopics.name: Barter, and types, characteristics and functions of money
subtopics.covers: Barter and its problems, the history and types of money, the characteristics of good money (2024 UTME Q14) and its functions.

subtopics.name: Demand for and supply of money
subtopics.covers: Motives for holding money (transactions, precautionary, speculative), what determines the money supply, and what the money supply consists of. How commercial banks create money goes to financial.deposit-banks.

subtopics.name: Value of money and the quantity theory
subtopics.covers: The relationship between the value of money and the price level, and the Fisher equation MV = PT, including solving it for one term.

subtopics.name: Meaning, types and causes of inflation
subtopics.covers: Demand-pull, cost-push, creeping, galloping and hyperinflation, and what causes each. A question on whether deficit financing is inflationary goes to public-finance.budget-debt. The Phillips curve goes to inflation.effects-control.

subtopics.name: Consumer price index
subtopics.covers: Calculating and interpreting a price index and the inflation rate from it.

subtopics.name: Effects and control of inflation
subtopics.covers: Who gains and who loses from inflation (debtors, creditors, fixed-income earners), how monetary, fiscal and direct measures control it, and the Phillips curve and the trade-off between inflation and unemployment, which neither syllabus names but the 2020 UTME tested (Q39). Every Phillips curve question goes here. A question that names a monetary instrument or stance (such as contractionary monetary policy) goes to financial.monetary-policy, and one that names a fiscal instrument goes to public-finance.fiscal-policy, even when the purpose is to control inflation; a question that asks how inflation can be controlled without naming an instrument goes here.

subtopics.name: Deflation
subtopics.covers: Meaning, measurement, effects and control of deflation.

subtopics.name: Types and functions of financial institutions
subtopics.covers: Traditional institutions (esusu, money lenders), development banks such as the Bank of Industry (2024 UTME Q33), merchant and mortgage banks, insurance companies and building societies: what each does, their role in development, and the challenges facing them in Nigeria. Commercial banks go to financial.deposit-banks and the CBN to financial.central-bank, but challenges facing banks in Nigeria, commercial banks included, go here.

subtopics.name: The Central Bank and financial regulation
subtopics.covers: Functions of the Central Bank of Nigeria, its officials (2024 UTME Q32), and financial sector regulators such as NDIC, SEC and NAICOM and what each does. The tools the CBN uses to control money go to financial.monetary-policy.

subtopics.name: Commercial banks and money creation
subtopics.covers: Functions of commercial (deposit money) banks, types of account, and how banks create credit, including calculating deposits created from a cash reserve ratio. Challenges facing banks in Nigeria go to financial.types.

subtopics.name: Money and capital markets
subtopics.covers: The difference between money and capital markets, their institutions and instruments (treasury bills, bonds, shares), and the stock exchange. Where a firm goes to raise funds goes to business.finance, even when the answer is the stock exchange.

subtopics.name: Monetary policy and its instruments
subtopics.covers: Open market operations, bank rate, reserve requirements, special deposits and moral suasion, expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, and their effects. A question that names a monetary instrument or stance goes here, even when its purpose is to control inflation; one that asks how inflation can be controlled without naming an instrument goes to inflation.effects-control. A question that asks which tool is fiscal and which monetary goes to public-finance.fiscal-policy.

subtopics.name: Objectives of public finance and fiscal policy
subtopics.covers: Meaning and objectives of public finance, fiscal policy and its instruments (taxation, spending, the budget), and telling fiscal from monetary tools (2024 UTME Q29).

subtopics.name: Government revenue and revenue allocation
subtopics.covers: Sources of government revenue (taxes, royalties, rents, fees, grants and aid), what hampers government's capacity to raise revenue, tax revenue included (evasion, corruption, a large informal sector, instability; 2018 UTME Q40), revenue allocation between tiers of government in Nigeria and its criteria, and resource control. A question on a specific tax goes to public-finance.taxation; a question on obstacles to raising tax revenue in general goes here.

subtopics.name: Taxation: types, canons and rates
subtopics.covers: Direct and indirect taxes, their objectives, merits and demerits, the canons of taxation, and proportional, progressive and regressive rates, including calculating tax paid. A question on what hampers government's capacity to raise tax revenue in general goes to public-finance.revenue.

subtopics.name: Incidence and effects of taxes
subtopics.covers: Who bears the burden of a tax, how elasticity of demand and supply shifts it between buyer and seller, and the effects of taxes on production and consumption.

subtopics.name: Public expenditure
subtopics.covers: Recurrent and capital expenditure, why public spending grows, and its effects on the economy.

subtopics.name: Government budget and public debt
subtopics.covers: Balanced, surplus and deficit budgets, deficit financing and its effect on prices (2024 UTME Q9), and internal and external public debt, its causes and burden.

subtopics.name: Basis of international trade
subtopics.covers: Differences between domestic and international trade, why countries trade, absolute and comparative advantage and working them out from a table, the theorists behind them (Smith, Ricardo, 2024 UTME Q5), and open and closed economies (whether a country trades with the rest of the world), which neither syllabus names but the 2020 UTME tested (Q38). Every question on whether an economy is open or closed goes here, even when the options include capitalist, socialist or mixed.

subtopics.name: Terms of trade
subtopics.covers: Meaning of terms of trade, calculating it from export and import price indices, and what favourable and unfavourable terms mean.

subtopics.name: Commercial policy and protection
subtopics.covers: Objectives of commercial policy, tariffs and their types, quotas, embargoes and other direct controls, arguments for and against protection, dumping (2024 UTME Q7), and trade liberalisation and globalisation as the opposite of protection. Using exchange rate changes to protect industry goes to bop.exchange-rate.

subtopics.name: Composition and direction of foreign trade
subtopics.covers: What Nigeria and other West African countries export and import, and who their main trading partners are. Dependence on a single export as a feature or problem of a developing economy (a mono-product economy) goes to development.problems.

topics.name: Balance of payments and exchange rates

subtopics.name: Balance of trade and balance of payments
subtopics.covers: Visible and invisible trade, the balance of trade, and the current, capital and monetary accounts of the balance of payments, including calculating a balance from given figures.

subtopics.name: Balance of payments problems and correction
subtopics.covers: Causes of balance of payments deficit and surplus, how a deficit is corrected (expenditure-reducing and switching policies, exchange control) and how it is financed (reserves, borrowing). Devaluation as a corrective measure goes to bop.exchange-rate.

subtopics.name: Exchange rates
subtopics.covers: Meaning, types (fixed, floating, managed) and determination of exchange rates, appreciation, depreciation and devaluation, and the conditions for depreciation to work, such as import elasticity (2024 UTME Q3 and Q4).

subtopics.name: Meaning, objectives and levels of integration
subtopics.covers: Free trade area, customs union, common market and economic union: their features, and the objectives and benefits of integration.

subtopics.name: ECOWAS and integration in West Africa
subtopics.covers: Formation, objectives, organs, achievements and problems of ECOWAS, and other African integration efforts. Every ECOWAS question goes here.

subtopics.name: IMF, World Bank and African Development Bank
subtopics.covers: The IMF, IBRD (World Bank) and AfDB: when they were set up, what they do, and their relevance to Nigeria and West Africa. UNCTAD, though JAMB lists it beside these, goes to organisations.others.

subtopics.name: UN, trade and regional bodies
subtopics.covers: UNCTAD, ECA, WTO, OECD, AU and the EU (EEC): functions and relevance, and telling regional from global bodies (2024 UTME Q28). Also the United Nations and its specialised agencies (such as WHO, FAO, ILO and UNESCO), which neither syllabus names but UTME papers test; every general UN question goes here. The IMF and World Bank go to organisations.finance, OPEC to natural-resources.oil and ECOWAS to integration.ecowas.

legacy_note: All 25 legacy database topics are broad: each names a whole syllabus topic or joins two or three of them. None matches a single subtopic, so every one is folded into the parent topic it fits best and none is guessed into a subtopic. A question moved to a parent is correct but unplaced within it, and is flagged for reclassification. Where a name spans several parents, the rule is the one its questions most likely test: 'Demand, supply and price determination' to price, where demand and supply meet; 'International trade, balance of payments and economic integration' to trade, its first and broadest part; 'Money and financial institutions' to money; 'Factors of production and division of labour' to factors; 'Contemporary economic problems and policies in West Africa' to development; and 'Structure of the West African economy' to basics, because the only place either syllabus describes the economy's structure is WAEC topic 1, the sectors and their contributions. These last four are judgement calls and their questions should be the first reclassified.
